prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: Quackies illustrated game BASE BOARD, no tokens or printed spaces.
Image1 is the authoritative edit target. Keep its chosen composition and clean painted cartoon style; make two focused improvements: equal clear path widths and a properly connected dramatic crossing into the wasteland.

A. MAKE ALL THREE ISLANDS' MAIN ROUTES BROAD ENOUGH FOR THE SAME GAME TILES:
The meadow's tall foliage has squeezed its left and right lanes. Pull this planting INWARD toward the island center, and compact the three shelter surrounds where necessary. The MAIN ROUTES across all three biomes should have approximately 120 pixels of usable clear width in this 1536x1024 composition, including bends, giving a 96-pixel-wide tile some breathing room. Treat this as a continuous clear corridor, not a few wide patches connected by narrow necks. Maintain broadly the same apparent width on left wetland, middle meadow and right desert. Keep route centerlines and U-shaped course close to this layout; widen into nonplayable inner planting and trim edge flowers, rocks, and reeds where they intrude. Do not merely lighten the overgrown path while leaving plants across it.
For the MIDDLE island especially, reserve calm short-grass lanes approximately x550–670 (left lane) and x865–985 (right lane) for most of their lengths y230–700. Pull the tall grass/flowers/branches on the inner edges into the x680–855 interior band. Allow subtle natural curvature but avoid pinches at the three shelter clusters. At the lower U bend keep roughly 120px deep open turf around y745–865; move the clumps projecting into the bend back into the central island or outside the corridor. Make the shelter vegetation compact enough for this, with modest inward shifts or slight scale adjustment permitted, but retain all three distinct cozy shelters and their order.
For the WETLAND keep the cool grassy loop equally generous, trimming reed tips and bank rocks from its lane centers while retaining the blue pond and existing scenery. For the DESERT keep its broad sandy loop comparable, moving any protruding little dead bushes/rock tips to the route edges. Large existing features stay in place. Do not expand the outside frame or flatten all three islands into rectangular tracks.
IMPORTANT: Preserve the dense continuous vegetation spine in the meadow interior, so one cannot shortcut straight across it or between bridges. Keep the wetland reed/willow barrier between the unfinished nest and bridge1. Do NOT solve width by removing the whole middle barrier. Three short dead-end meadow shelter entrances remain open: top shelter access to LEFT lane; middle stone shelter access to RIGHT lane; bottom shelter access DOWN to bottom bend. There must be an obvious connection from each bowl to that lane. Keep the final corridors calm, low-detail and free of foreground leaves, tall grasses, shrubs, boulders and tree shadows that resemble obstacles.

B. A DRAMATIC, CONNECTED WASTELAND BRIDGE:
Replace ONLY the SECOND crossing (meadow to right-hand desert) with a more dramatic weathered timber-and-rope footbridge across the rocky cleft. Show a deeper shadowed chasm directly under the deck, jagged rock shoulders, stout anchored timber posts and curved rope handrails. It should signal entering harsh terrain while remaining continuous and comfortably traversable: NO missing boards, holes or barricades.
Fix the geometry of its approaches: the meadow's right-hand UPWARD lane should curve smoothly onto the bridge's OPEN LEFT end; the OPEN RIGHT end should land on an ochre rock/sand shoulder that curves smoothly down into the desert's left-hand DOWNWARD lane. These two approaches must visually touch the actual deck ends at the same ground level, not end against a side rail or post. A gentle diagonal left-high/right-low deck angle is welcome if it makes the route connection more natural; keep the crossing in its current top-of-cleft location. Give the deck convincing supported/anchored endpoints, contact shadows and a continuous grassy-to-worn-wood-to-sand sequence. Keep rope rails along the crossing's two sides, not across either entrance. The dramatic cleft should be local to this crossing and should not eat into the lower meadow lane's width.
Preserve the FIRST wetland bridge's newer grounded timber-and-stone design and natural approaches.

OTHER INVARIANTS:
Same three-biome layout, cool teal wetland / warm sunny green grassland / barren ochre wasteland; unfinished empty nest at upper LEFT; all eight shelters in2/3/3 distribution; waterfall oasis at far upper RIGHT; same outer rounded wooden frame and clean blank cream footer. Keep the illustration crisp: deliberate smooth leaf and grass shapes, clean outlines and controlled painted shading, no added speckle/grain, no blurry repeated microtexture. No redesign of the desert scene beyond path-edge clearance and bridge connection.
ABSOLUTELY NO tiles, pads, tokens, ducks, labels, numbers, currency, arrows, text or legend. Base artwork only.
